title: MAINT: Add wrappers to `write_espresso_ph` and `read_espresso_ph`
body: I added the `@reader` wrapper to `read_espresso_ph` and the `@writer` wrapper to `write_espresso_ph` as I got an error message using those two functions.
author: ollyeh01

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @ollyeh01 for the MR! Yes, with these wrappers, these functions can now accept not only file objects but also filenames.

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body:
@yuzie007 --- this breaks some things. Now `write_espresso_ph` requires a positional argument `file`. Just wanted to let you know.

```
>               write_espresso_ph(fd=fd, properties=properties, **parameters)
E               TypeError: write_espresso_ph() missing 1 required positional argument: 'file'
```

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @AndrewRosen for the report! OK, the reason is the inconsistency of the first argument name with [here](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/utils/__init__.py?ref_type=heads#L591).

For typical ASE `read/write` methods that return `Atoms`, I would probably say it should be a positional argument that users should not rely on the argument name, but now I noticed `read_espresso_ph/write_espresso_ph` are probably auxiliary functions specifically for phonon calculations with QE. Would you think it is better or safer to revert? (I am inclining to do.)

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: @ollyeh01 It may also depend on what type of error message you have seen.

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body: Admittedly, I do not know enough about Espresso to say either way. I just caught it in my test suites. I'll leave it to you but wanted to make you aware.
